purpose: Document Oita first-party cadastral-program discovery, public map portal inspection, Ministry of Justice registry-map catalog inspection, request outcomes, safety limits and runtime qualification status.
assessment: Oita City's official cadastral-survey page evidences local cadastral work and points to the national survey-status map. The public Oita Map landing/configuration was fetched but did not expose a verified cadastral parcel API. G-Space CKAN metadata lists Ministry of Justice Oita registry-map XML archives, but no bounded safe-ID geometry response was obtained; no sample was retained and runtime readiness remains held.
registryAssessment: Local cadastral custody/program evidence is present, but this packet does not admit an anonymous citywide parcel runtime source.

officialPrimarySources.observation: Oita City describes cadastral surveying as creating cadastral maps and ledgers for parcel land information and links to the national survey-status map.
Public Oita Map landing/configuration was fetched; no verified cadastral parcel layer/API was identified.
G-Space catalog identifies Oita City (Oita Legal Affairs Bureau) registry-office map data and 44201-3200-2024/2025 ZIP resources.
Anonymous CKAN API returned HTTP 200 metadata; both listed Oita resources are large ZIP/XML archives of approximately 314 MB.
Public G-Space documentation lists Oita among available converted registry-map datasets and explains the conversion caveat; no bounded feature was retained.
Official Oita Legal Affairs Bureau notice about registry-office map creation in named Oita districts; not a public parcel API.
